text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm handing off primary at 18:00 UTC to @jon. I'll be reachable for the first 10m after handoff but have a meeting at 18:30. Primary: jon. Secondary: ashley. :wave:

maria: Notes: there's a scheduled model push at 19:00 UTC (canary first). If you get pager noise during the deploy, follow the deploy runbook linked below and favor safe rollback for correctness-impacting regressions.

maria: Quick checklist for the handoff: 
- Confirm PD routing (primary -> secondary -> eng-lead). 
- Verify runbook version at /runbooks/inference/serving-deploy.md (last updated 2026-02-18).
- Watch the latency dashboard (console > routes > generation) for 95th pct spikes.

devops-bot: Reminder: scheduled deploy window 19:00-19:20 UTC. Auto-scaling config locked for window.

jon: Thanks — pinged PD to confirm routing. Two questions: 1) There's a coverage gap 20:00-21:00 where my signal will be weak (travel). Can ashley cover that hour as primary? 2) Any open incidents I should be aware of?

maria: No active Sev incidents right now. We had a small KV cache eviction flurry earlier but that resolved automatically. For 20:00-21:00 — I can cover 20:00-20:15 then jump back at 21:00. If ashley is available, she'd be primary 20:15-20:45?

ashley: I can cover 20:15-21:00 but have a calendar block 20:30-20:50 that I can't reschedule. If jon is reachable by phone we can split: ashley primary 20:15-20:30, jon primary 20:30-21:00. Not ideal though.

jon: I can do 20:30-21:00 from phone if needed. Are we comfortable with split? I can route urgent PD alerts to my phone.

maria: Let's avoid split if possible. @eng-lead can you confirm a short coverage swap? If not, we'll accept the split and update PD notes.

eng-lead: I can take 20:00-20:30. That avoids the split. I'm happy to be the backup for the deploy window too if things get noisy.

maria: Perfect — updated: primary schedule: 
- 18:00-20:00 jon (primary) 
- 20:00-20:30 eng-lead (primary) 
- 20:30-21:00 ashley (primary) 
Secondary: whoever is not primary for that slot. I'll update the oncall doc after this thread.

jon: Thanks. Now escalation rules — let's confirm so there's no confusion during high-severity events. I put a short snippet below that we can paste into PD escalation steps.

jon: ```Escalation flow (production inference):
1) Page primary (pagerduty: primary_oncall) immediately for S0/S1
2) If no ack in 3m, page secondary
3) If still no ack in 8m total or issue is system-wide (>=3 customer impact reports), page eng-lead and infra@team (pagerduty: eng-lead)
4) If incident classified S0 and >10m of customer-facing error rate, mobilize incident manager and exec notify
Notes: for latency-only regressions with no 5xx spike, prefer quick mitigation (scaling, degrade non-critical routes) over full rollback.```

maria: Agree. Add: for model-quality regressions (generation gibberish, hallucinations) treat as S1: page primary, attach eval run id, and escalate to model-oncall if available.

ashley: For paging thresholds, threshold settings we use are: 
- Error-rate: >2% 5xx sustained for 5m -> page S1
- Latency: p95 > 1200ms for traffic baseline for 5m -> page S2 (unless customer-impacting)
- CPU/GPU throttling: any node OOMs or GPU memory errors -> page S1

incident-bot: Auto-detection rule triggered: p95 latency spike on route /v1/generate between 19:03-19:07 UTC; delta +650ms. Alert created: INC-2026-492.

jon: Got the bot alert. I'm watching metrics now. If it stays >5m I'll escalate per flow. Can someone check the canary logs for model-load errors? 

maria: I'll pull logs. Quick grep: ```kubectl logs -l app=redwood-serving -n prod --tail=200 | grep -i 'kv cache'``` found intermittent cache hit drops but no OOMs.

eng-lead: I can shadow logs and join PD incident if it escalates. If you need me to take over primary, say so.

jon: Thanks. Action items while I triage: 
- maria: keep watching canary and logs (assigned)
- ashley: standby to take PD if primary misses ack (assigned)
- eng-lead: standby for escalation (assigned)

maria: Also adding runbook pointer for quick rollback during deploy: 
```Steps to rollback canary -> stable:
1) Disable canary route: infra console > routing > disable canary
2) Revert model tag in deployment to previous SHA: kubectl patch deployment redwood-model --patch '{"spec": {"template": {"metadata": {"annotations": {"model-sha":"prev-sha"}}}}}'
3) Monitor p95 and error-rate for 10m
4) If stable, re-run canary after investigating root cause
```

jon: Noted. Also, please update PD incident notes with who is primary/secondary and any coverage swaps so paging works. I'll acknowledge the bot alert and start a triage timeline in the incident ticket.

maria: TL;DR for whoever reads this later: handoff done; primary is jon until 20:00; eng-lead will cover 20:00-20:30; ashley 20:30-21:00. Escalation flow: page primary -> 3m -> secondary -> 8m -> eng-lead -> incident manager for S0. Runbooks and rollback steps linked above.

ashley: Sounds good. Please ping in #incidents if anything changes.

jon: Acknowledged. Taking primary now. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: Handoff recorded in oncall log. 

maria: Thanks team — I'll update the oncall doc and PD notes, then step out.
